title: Stem changes in all forms, colgar, Arabic words, tomar, we (-amos)

cards.title: The split happens in most forms
cards.body: Querer: quiero, quiere, quieren, quieres. Perder: pierdo, pierde, pierden, pierdes.

cards.title: Not always: experiment
cards.body: Comer → como doesn't split. There's no way to know in advance; try it, get feedback, and your intuition develops.

cards.title: colgar = to hang
cards.body: Go back to the 'to' form (colgar, -ar) to avoid 'cuelge'.

cards.title: al- words come from Arabic
cards.body: Al- means 'the' in Arabic and is written as part of the word, so these words came in with it attached: alcohol is literally 'the alcohol'.

cards.title: tomar = to take / to drink
cards.body: Tomar is 'to take' and is also used for drinking.

cards.title: azúcar, arroz — al- that blended in
cards.body: In Arabic, the l of al- blends into many following sounds, giving azúcar (sugar) and arroz (rice, from al-ruz). English took these words without the 'the'. Spanish never writes ss, but rr marks the rolled r.

cards.title: More Arabic in Spanish
cards.body: Southern Spain was part of the Muslim world for about 800 years, so Spanish has many Arabic words English lacks.

cards.title: ¿Qué tomas? and beber
cards.body: ¿Qué tomas? can mean 'what are you having to drink?'. Beber also means to drink; una bebida = a drink.

cards.title: we = -amos
cards.body: Take off -ar and add -amos. The stress moves: toMAmos, haBLAmos.

cards.title: No stress, no split
cards.body: In the we form the root vowel isn't stressed, so it doesn't split.

cards.title: Pienso que sí; ¿qué piensas hacer?
cards.body: 'I think so' = 'I think that yes'. '¿Qué piensas hacer?' = what do you plan to do?

examples.en: What do you plan to do?

practice.why: No split in the we form.

practice.en: What do you (informal) plan to do?
